title.narrative: Capacity Building to Electricidade de Moçambique (EDM) & strategic studies
Kapacitetsuppbyggnad till Electricidad de Moçambique(EDM) & strategiska studier

description.narrative:
Det övergripande målet med kapacitetsuppbyggnadsprogrammet är att göra det möjligt för EDM att bygga upp sin kapacitet inom områdena förbättrade kommersiella och finansiella resultat, intern ledning och kontroll samt en hållbar utveckling av företagets organisation och mänskliga resurser.
Förväntade resultat är: • Införande av International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) • Förbättrad ekonomisk hållbarhet • Minskat antal kvalifikationer i revisionsberättelser • Minskning av icke-tekniska förluster
Det övergripande målet med de strategiska studierna är att bidra till en förbättrad strategisk planering för en fortsatt ökad tillgång till säker energi och en allmän hållbar utveckling av sektorn.
Förväntade resultat är: • Utveckling av strategiska planer inom sektorn i linje med prioriteringarna i den svenska samarbetsstrategin med Moçambique, 2008-2012 • Utveckling eller up-dates av studier för identifiering av energiprojekt • Utveckling av förstudier för prioriterade projekt inom sektorn

The overall objective of the Capacity Building Program is to enable EDM to building up their capacity within the areas of improved commercial and financial performance, internal management and control and sustained development of the organisation and human resources of the company.
Expected results are: • Introduction of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) • Improved financial sustainability • Reduced number of qualifications in auditor’s reports • Reduction of non-technical losses
The overall objective of the Strategic Studies is to contribute to an improved strategic planning for a continued increase in access to secure energy and a general sustainable development of the sector.
Expected results are: • Development of strategic plans in the sector in line with priorities set in the Swedish Cooperation Strategy with Mozambique, 2008-2012 • Development or up-dates of studies for identification of energy projects • Development of feasibility studies for prioritized projects in the sector

The agreement which was signed in 2010 and has been amended six times due to the dynamics and necessities at EDM, has two key aspects, the capacity building component and the strategic studies component. The agreement period terminated on the 30th of June 2024 with the activity period ending on the 31st of December 2023. 1. Capacity building: the main objective of the Program is to provide sustainable energy for poverty reduction. The specific objectives are to enable EDM to provide sufficient, affordable and reliable electricity for the purpose of economic growth, improved delivery of public goods through improved capacity and to support strategic planning for a sustainable development of the energy sector. This (initial) CBP program had two separate but linked projects: Project A: Business and Process Development and Management, aiming to further develop EDM business areas and work processes to achieve improvements in the areas addressed, resulting in improved overall performance. Project B: Human Resources Development (HRD), to provide EDM staff with general and specific skills at various levels in a number of areas, including management. As the budget for Human Resources Development in Project B was primarily used to develop a training plan, the Embassy agreed to allocate additional funds for training activities for EDM staff focusing on two priority areas: 1) Procurement; and 2) Risk assessment in relation to Safety and Occupational Health and Environment. A further initiative as part of the transformation process with links to the CBP was the introduction of e-learning in the organization as an effective way to spread the Code of Ethics, adopted by the EDM Board in 2017, but also as a means to increase equal access to training opportunities in the organization and strengthen awareness of gender and environmental issues as a first step. The covid-19 pandemic also increased the necessity for e-learning since physical training was not possible. 2. Strategic Studies: the specific objective is to support strategic planning for sustainable development of the energy sector. The decision memorandum more specifically spells out the overall objective of the Strategic Studies to contribute to an improved strategic planning for a continued increase in access to secure energy and a general sustainable development of the sector. Expected results are: a) Development of strategic plans in the sector in line with priorities set in the Swedish Cooperation Strategy with Mozambique b) Development or up-dates of studies for identification of energy projects c) Development of feasibility studies for prioritized projects in the sector

title.narrative: Decision on contribution EDM Capacity Building Strategic Studies

description.narrative: The main results of the CBP are as follows: - The review of commercial work processes has served as an input to the implementation of the EDM integrated management system (Sistema Integrado de Gestao da EDM, SIGEM) and Implementation of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is now performed by EDM independently. - An updated Meter Policy and an Automated Meter Reading System (MV90) Maintenance Manual (an Operators Handbook for daily/weekly/monthly operational tasks in running the MV90 system) have been produced and training performed. - Metering quality equipment from Unipower has been purchased and training performed. - A draft Loss Reduction Plan has been formulated and a Losses Database constructed. Six single-user software licenses of Navicat Postgres to efficiently handle the Losses Database have been purchased. - An Energy Efficiency (EE) strategy; an EE Awareness strategy; a Directional Policy Matrix (DPM) strategy and a Demand Side Management (DSM) strategy have been formulated, as well as a ToR for EE implementation support - Part of the training plan was implemented (with additional financing) - Reallocation to other more focused project activities like procurement and Safety, Occupational Health, and Environmental issues (SOHE) produced better results - Failure by consultants to install a functioning e-learning platform was rectified internally which has strengthened capacity and confidence to move ahead with development of digital training and development of e-learning courses Summary of indicator results for the capacity building component: As mentioned above the improved capacities of EDM as an institution and for its staff were meant to improve service to the customers. Below are the results from the various activities: - total Energy sold per year of 2700 GWh (Giga Watt Hours) by 2012 but this number reached 3900GWH in 2012 - Through the improvement of business and internal work processes it was expected that by 2012 the ratio of MWH/staff (Megawatt hours sold/staff da EDM) would be 677 but this has since risen to 2327 by 2021. - As a result of the development of human resources, building and maintenance of capabilities and improved performance, the ratio of EDM customers to staff employed by the company was expected to be 230 by 2012 but this rose to 328 by 2012 and 883 by 2024. 1. SAIDI = System Average Interruption Duration Index, was 28h in 2012 but is now 0.26h currently 2. SAIFI = System Average Interruption Frequency Index, was 30h in 2012 and now has gone down to 0.77h 3. No. of days to treat complaints, this has also been reduced to a time of three hours currently. 4. No. of days for new connection, there is no record for 2012 but it is noted that the time for a new connection has been drastically reduced to three days from the time of request With respect to the reduction in losses: - It was planned to have a maximum total of 28% of losses (distribution and non-technical losses) and 26% was achieved in 2012 which also included transmission and 24% in 2024. - Furthermore, a specific directorate for revenue protection (DPRP) was created, to facilitate and monitor all issues related to non-technical losses. Summary of results for the strategic studies component: Several studies were carried out during the implementation of this component and the reports approved both by EDM and the Embassy of Sweden. 1. The feasibility study of the Tsate hydropower plant was completed but since the process has taken a long time the cost of implementation has significantly gone up and EDM has yet to look for funding for the project. Sweden by a government decision of 4 December 2025 will support the Mozambican government through a bilateral cooperation agreement only until August 31st of 2026 hence cannot fund the project. Furthermore, the other donors (EU and KfW) have decided not to go ahead with the project due to the increased costs. 2. Feasibility study of the rehabilitation of the Corumana power plant was also successfully completed but up to now EDM has not secured financing for the project. 3. The Environmental and social impact assessment of the Nampula Angoche transmission line project was also successfully completed. The European Investment Bank has committed to provide a loan and the EU together with KfW the German bank will provide grant funding for the implementation of the project. This project will be implemented as a package together with Massinga Vilanculos transmission line of which feasibility and Environmental studies were also funded by Sweden. 4. Feasibility of the electrification of Mozambican administrative posts was also completed, and the results are being adapted in the ongoing electrification projects. The launch of the e-learning platform by EDM which was financed by Sida has also brought savings of up to $450 000 annually since EDM does not have to move its employees from other areas of the country to Maputo training center for the various training courses which have already been incorporated on the platform especially the one on safety issues at the workplace.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
